discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
motivation: Kane and Mele (2005) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new, time-reversal-protected topological state of matter. They introduced the Z2 invariant, which separates the quantum spin Hall insulator from ordinary band insulators and guarantees helical edge states that are robust against nonmagnetic disorder. Molenkamp's group achieved the decisive experiment in 2007. After years of improving the growth of HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, they observed quantized edge conductance above the predicted critical thickness, which established the first two-dimensional topological insulator. Together these works opened the field of topological insulators. They led directly to three-dimensional topological insulators, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, topological superconductivity and proposals for dissipationless electronics and fault-tolerant quantum computation. This is an outstanding example of theoretical insight and painstaking materials control together uncovering a new, universal principle of quantum matter.
